lead: Fort Lauderdale plumbing deals with a high water table, king tides, heavy rain and aging cast-iron drains. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Fort Lauderdale.
risk: cast-iron drain failures, flooding and backups, and slab leaks
risk_short: cast-iron drains, flooding and slab leaks
why: Victoria Park, Rio Vista and Coral Ridge have many homes from the 1940s to the 1970s with cast-iron drains under the slab that are rotting from the inside. Lining or replacing them is a common job.
The April 2023 storm dropped more than 25 inches of rain in a day and flooded much of the city. King tides push water up through storm drains in low areas near the canals.
utility: City of Fort Lauderdale Public Works
water: Fort Lauderdale pumps its water from the Biscayne Aquifer and treats it at the city's plants. It is moderately hard.
tips: Have cast-iron drains scoped in older homes.
Shut off the main valve before a hurricane evacuation.
Know your flood zone and king tide dates.
Check condo rules before plumbing work.
areas: PipeMend works in Victoria Park, Las Olas, Rio Vista, Coral Ridge, Harbor Beach, Flagler Village, Imperial Point and every other neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Fort Lauderdale Development Services Department, and plumbing contractors are licensed by the Florida Construction Industry Licensing Board.

faq.q: Why do older Fort Lauderdale homes have drain problems?
faq.a: Many have cast-iron drains under the slab. Decades of use and Florida's climate corrode them from the inside, causing slow drains, backups and smells. A camera inspection shows what is needed.
